transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello. To be honest, once I start eating, especially at night after work, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed, and I knew I needed to seek some help.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever do things to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives, but I do try to make up for it in other ways. The next day, I'll punish myself by drinking only coffee all day, or I'll force myself to walk laps around the local fairgrounds or parking lots until my knees ache. I just feel this intense need to burn off the food and compensate for what I did.
How many times a week do these episodes of overeating and compensating usually happen, and how many months has this been going on?

This cycle of overeating and then starving myself or walking for hours happens at least once or twice a week. It's been going on for about four months now, ever since my new sales initiative at work really ramped up.
How do you feel about your body shape and weight, and does a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat influence how you value yourself as a person?

It has a massive impact on how I value myself. When I'm at work or client dinners, I constantly worry about how big I look in my suits, and if the scale is up even a single pound in the morning, I feel like a complete failure as a person and at my job, no matter how good my sales numbers are.
Could you tell me your current height and weight, and whether you have a specific target weight you are trying to stay below?

I don't know my exact weight right now, and I try not to focus on a specific target number. I just know that I feel like I've gotten too big for my professional suits, and if the scale goes up even by a single pound, I feel like a complete failure.
Over the last three months, have these episodes of overeating and compensating happened at least twice every single week, or are there weeks where they only occur once?

It varies depending on how stressful my week at work is. Some weeks it only happens once, but on the busier and more stressful weeks, it definitely happens twice. Overall, it has been happening at least once or twice every single week for the past few months.
Do you have a specific maximum weight that you absolutely refuse to go over, and is that number significantly lower than what a doctor would consider healthy for your height?

I don't really have a specific maximum weight or a number in mind that I absolutely refuse to go over. It is more that I feel a general sense of panic and failure whenever the scale goes up even a little bit. I just can't stand seeing that number increase at all, no matter what it is.
Outside of the actual overeating episodes, do you find yourself constantly preoccupied with thoughts of food or experiencing an irresistible craving to eat throughout the day?

I don't really experience constant cravings or an irresistible urge to eat during the day. Instead, my thoughts are consumed by worrying about my weight and feeling guilty about what I ate the night before. I spend most of the day planning how to restrict my food or walk it off to make up for it.
On average over the last three months, would you say these episodes of overeating and compensating have occurred at least twice a week, or has the average been closer to once a week?

I'd say the average is at least once or twice a week over the last three months. Ever since my new sales role ramped up, there hasn't been a week where I haven't had at least one of these out-of-control nights followed by trying to make up for it the next day.
Have you ever in the past experienced a period where you were severely underweight, or have you ever been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa?
No, I have never been severely underweight in the past. I have also never been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa.
During these episodes of overeating, do you eat an amount of food that is definitely much larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time, say within two hours?

Yes, I absolutely do. There are evenings where I’ll sit in my car after a long workday and eat through two entire drive-thru meals, a big bag of chips, and candy before I even go inside my house. It's like I'm on autopilot, and I just can't stop eating until I feel completely stuffed and sick.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you strictly limited your food intake and lost a significant amount of weight, even if you weren't considered severely underweight?

No, I haven't really had a period in my life where I strictly restricted my food and lost a significant amount of weight. While I do try to strictly diet or skip meals for a day to compensate after overeating, it has never resulted in any major weight loss.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors (fasting and excessive walking) occurring at least once or twice a week for four months. While she experiences a morbid dread of fatness and significant overvaluation of weight, she does not meet the full ICD-10 criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) because she denies constant food cravings/preoccupation throughout the day and does not have a sharply defined weight threshold. Therefore, the clinical presentation is best classified as Atypical Bulimia Nervosa (F50.3).
